title: Superseded sibling DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA hardcodes the DEAD SYA (0x3bBE) and reads an empty deployments file — latent wrong-route footgun adjacent to 2.3
description: The saga-2 retirement surface that 2.3 owns has a superseded sibling, DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol, that performs the same removeYieldStrategy / SYA-deregister operation. That sibling hardcodes `LIVE_SYA=0x3bBE928340c61a65Cb6C4a87B3fb59B6f3F7606a` — the DEAD pre-story-058 SYA, superseded by the live `0x3C690EC3...8270` — and reads the empty ys-swap-deployments.json. 2.3 itself uses the correct live SYA `0x3C69` and is the route in the npm flow; this is the residual cross-route hazard adjacent to 2.3, NOT a 2.3 defect. Surfaced under the same-surface exception (reachable from the saga-2 retirement surface 2.3 owns), not an unrelated scope.
impact: None on the saga-2 flow itself — 2.3 uses the correct live SYA and is the npm route. The superseded sibling, if run, accomplishes nothing (reverts on empty JSON or no-ops against the dead 0x3bBE instance); no value is moved, lost, or stolen. The defect is a non-obvious cross-route operator footgun: because 0x3bBE may still retain code and a matching owner, the `owner()`/`code.length` preflight is not a guaranteed loud failure, so an operator who picks the wrong, superseded retirement route can believe the old strategies were deregistered when they were not.
attackPath: 1. Operator picks the superseded ys-swap DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol instead of (or in addition to) 2.3.
2. It hardcodes LIVE_SYA=0x3bBE (the DEAD pre-story-058 SYA) and reads the empty ys-swap-deployments.json.

3. The empty-JSON read reverts in practice, OR — since 0x3bBE may still have code and a matching owner — the owner()/code.length preflight is not a guaranteed loud failure and it no-ops against the dead instance.
4. Operator believes the old strategies were deregistered when they were not.
recommendation: Quarantine or repoint the superseded sibling: remove DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol from the cluster, or update its hardcoded LIVE_SYA constant to the live `0x3C690EC3...8270` and point it at a populated inputs file, so a wrong-route operator cannot silently no-op a believed deregistration. No change needed to 2.3 itself.
evidence: Fork-verified (script-auditor, run-18): 2.3 targets the correct live SYA 0x3C69 and is the npm route; the superseded sibling DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol (L50-52) still ships unquarantined with LIVE_SYA=0x3bBE (dead pre-story-058 SYA) and an empty ys-swap-deployments.json.

The wrong-route hazard here is that an operator silently no-ops a believed deregistration against the dead instance. Surfaced as a residual cross-route hazard adjacent to 2.3 (same-surface exception), NOT a 2.3 defect.
